ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Option (A) shows y(t) as a constant rectangle from t=0 to 2T_s, with height labeled 1/T_s; option (B) shows a trapezoid that rises from 0 to 0.5, maintains a plateau, and then falls to 0, with support interval approximately from 0 to 2T_s; option (C) shows a triangle that rises linearly from t=0, reaches the peak value 1 at t=T_s, and then falls linearly to 0 at t=2T_s; option (D) shows a triangle from t=0 to t=T_s, with peak value 1 at t=T_s/2. Reasoning: It is known that p(t)=1/sqrt(T_s), 0<=t<=T_s, otherwise 0. The impulse response of the matched filter is h(t)=p(T_s-t). Since this rectangular pulse, after being reversed with respect to the interval, is still located at 0<=t<=T_s, h(t) is also a rectangle with height 1/sqrt(T_s) and width T_s. The output y(t)=p(t)*h(t). During convolution, the overlap length of two rectangles with width T_s increases linearly from 0 to T_s within 0<t<T_s, and decreases linearly from T_s to 0 within T_s<t<2T_s. Then multiplying by the amplitude factor (1/sqrt(T_s))^2=1/T_s gives y(t)=t/T_s, 0<=t<=T_s; y(t)=(2T_s-t)/T_s, T_s<=t<=2T_s. Therefore the output is a triangle with support interval from 0 to 2T_s and peak value 1 at T_s, corresponding to option (C) in the image.

method.method_draft: Describe the image options, then compute in the time domain. From the text, read p(t)=1/sqrt(T_s) on 0<=t<=T_s and zero otherwise. Form the matched filter h(t)=p(T_s-t), which is again 1/sqrt(T_s) on 0<=t<=T_s. Compute y(t)=p(t)*h(t): the overlap length increases linearly from 0 to T_s for 0<t<T_s and decreases linearly from T_s to 0 for T_s<t<2T_s. Multiplying by (1/sqrt(T_s))^2 gives y(t)=t/T_s on [0,T_s] and y(t)=(2T_s-t)/T_s on [T_s,2T_s], so the graph is a triangle of support 0 to 2T_s with peak 1 at T_s. Match this to graph C.
